lines.speaker: wick
lines.text: Main Street. The bakery's the only thing open. It's always the only thing open.

lines.speaker: wick
lines.text: Don't ask what they bake at night. I asked once. They said "tomorrow."
Locked. A sign hangs in the window.
"Night only. You don't have a card."
Warm light. Rows and rows of bread that does not exist yet.
Closed. Everything in there is asleep, even the price tags.
A bench. Cold. Benches are always cold at night. It's their whole thing.
The corner mailbox. Something inside it is breathing very softly. Probably letters.

lines.speaker: postman
lines.text: You can see me. That's new.

lines.speaker: postman
lines.text: I deliver dreams. One envelope a house, under the pillow, before three.
In his bag, one envelope glows a little brighter than the rest. It has your name on it.

lines.speaker: postman
lines.text: You get it when you're asleep. That's the rule.

lines.speaker: postman
lines.text: And you are very much not asleep.

lines.speaker: postman
lines.text: ...still not asleep, I see. The letter can wait. Letters are good at waiting.
